title: Perf/pytorch block fp8 moe decode
body:
## Motivation

The existing PyTorch Block-FP8 MoE path may launch GEMM CTAs for every local
expert during small-batch decode, even though only a small subset of experts
receives tokens. For example, with `M=1`, `top-k=8`, and `E=256`, at most eight
experts are active while the original dense expert grid still covers all 256
experts.

The activation path also materializes the BF16 SwiGLU result before launching
a separate FP8 quantization kernel:

```text
gate/up GEMM
  -> silu_and_mul
  -> BF16 intermediate
  -> quant_fp8
  -> FP8 down-projection input
```

This PR reduces both the inactive-expert launch overhead and the intermediate
activation traffic in Block-FP8 MoE decode.

## Modification

### Active-expert block scheduling

Add an opt-in active-block dispatch:

```bash
LMDEPLOY_MOE_ACTIVE_BLOCK_DECODE=1
```

The path reuses the existing compact MoE kernel and routed-block metadata, but
launches GEMM programs only for expert blocks that receive tokens.

Dispatch is selected using backend properties only:

- GPU compute capability
- input and output dtype
- FP8 group size
- token count
- expert count and top-k
- hidden and local projection dimensions

There are no model-name checks. Unknown or unsupported shapes retain the
existing schedule. The optimization also falls back for unsupported expert
layouts, dtypes, GPUs, and tensor shapes.

### Fused SwiGLU and FP8 quantization

Fuse `silu_and_mul` with group-wise FP8 quantization for the default Block-FP8
MoE activation:

```text
gate/up GEMM
  -> silu_and_mul_post_quant
  -> FP8 activation + scale
  -> down-projection GEMM
```

This removes one kernel launch and avoids materializing and rereading the BF16
activation. Custom activation functions continue using the existing fallback.

## Performance

### End-to-end active-block scheduling

Environment:

- 8 x NVIDIA H200
- PyTorch engine
- TP=8, EP=1
- CUDA Graph enabled
- Block-FP8 MoE model
- input length 128, output length 256
- symmetric-memory AllReduce baseline
- one warm-up and five measured repeats; median reported

| Concurrency | Baseline TPOT | Active TPOT | TPOT reduction | Baseline tok/s | Active tok/s | Throughput gain |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 20.023 ms | 17.527 ms | 12.47% | 48.371 | 55.053 | 13.82% |
| 4 | 21.147 ms | 18.769 ms | 11.24% | 183.429 | 205.707 | 12.14% |

The baseline and candidate both used the fused SwiGLU/quant path, so this table
isolates the contribution of active-block scheduling.

### SwiGLU and FP8 quantization microbenchmark

The benchmark used the TP8 local routed-MoE shape with `top-k=8` and local
intermediate size 256.

| Decode M | Separate kernels | Fused kernel | Latency reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 7.403 us | 5.466 us | 26.17% |
| 4 | 7.565 us | 5.424 us | 28.30% |
| 16 | 7.690 us | 5.777 us | 24.87% |
| 32 | 7.892 us | 5.861 us | 25.74% |

This is an operator-level result and is not added directly to the end-to-end
active-block gain.

## BC-breaking

No backward-incompatible API changes are introduced.

The active-block schedule is opt-in, and unsupported shapes fall back to the
existing implementation. The fused activation preserves the established
custom-activation fallback.

## Correctness and validation

- The fused FP8 activation is bitwise equal to
  `quant_fp8(silu_and_mul(x))` for the measured shapes.
- The generated FP8 scales are bitwise equal.
- Greedy end-to-end output digests matched across all measured repeats.
- Existing kernel tests pass: `97 passed`.
- `py_compile` and `git diff --check` pass.

Commands:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/pytorch/kernel/test_activation.py \
  tests/pytorch/kernel/test_fused_moe.py

python -m py_compile \
  lmdeploy/pytorch/kernels/cuda/activation.py \
  lmdeploy/pytorch/kernels/cuda/moe/blocked_fp8.py

git diff --check
```

title: refactor: stream tool parameters incrementally
body:
## Motivation

The existing tool-call parsing pipeline maintains separate streaming and complete parsing paths. Several model-specific parsers also buffer or repeatedly scan accumulated payloads before emitting arguments. This causes:

- delayed tool-argument delivery;
- inconsistent behavior between streaming and non-streaming responses;
- results that depend on engine chunk boundaries, especially around closing tags, incomplete payloads, and adjacent tool calls;
- duplicated JSON/XML parsing logic and unclear ownership between response parsers and tool parsers;
- quadratic scanning in some large JSON payloads containing many short strings.

This PR introduces one low-overhead incremental parsing model with clear module boundaries. Stable tool-call fragments are emitted as soon as possible, while an argument that appears before its function name is retained until the call identity is known. Downstream consumers remain responsible for validating argument semantics.

## Modification

- Introduce a consumed-prefix interface for tool parsers:
  - `ToolParser.feed_tool_block()` consumes only stable input and returns the number of characters that the response parser may discard.
  - `ResponseParser` owns reasoning/content/tool boundaries and retained input.
  - Concrete tool parsers own their inner payload grammar.
- Unify streaming and complete parsing:
  - `BaseResponseParser.parse_complete()` reuses the streaming state machine.
  - Streaming and non-streaming responses therefore share malformed/incomplete-payload semantics.
  - Newlines used only to separate adjacent tool blocks are no longer exposed as assistant content.
- Define a normalized streaming contract:
  - the first visible delta for an accepted tool call contains its ID, type, index, and function name;
  - arguments encountered before the function name are buffered and emitted immediately after the identity;
  - argument fragments, including duplicate parameter keys, are preserved in source order;
  - generated function names absent from `request.tools` are consistently filtered.
- Add shared incremental JSON infrastructure:
  - introduce `JsonToolParser` for Qwen, InternLM, and Llama JSON envelopes;
  - introduce `JsonValueScanner` to locate streamed JSON value boundaries without validating or reserializing the payload;
  - optimize scanning of large JSON containers to avoid repeatedly searching the same suffix;
  - consolidate Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 parsing under `Qwen3ToolParser`.
- Refactor XML-like parsing:
  - introduce an explicit shared state machine in `XmlToolParser`;
  - keep syntax recognition in GLM/Qwen-derived parsers while centralizing argument streaming, JSON construction, and schema-based value coercion;
  - retain only tokenizer-valid closing-marker prefixes across chunks.
- Refactor DeepSeek DSML and Kimi parsers to use the same incremental emission and consumed-prefix contract.
- Correct metadata fan-out when one engine chunk produces multiple parser deltas:
  - token IDs and logprobs are attached only once;
  - unnecessary empty SSE deltas are suppressed.
- Expand regression coverage for split markers, large arguments, duplicate parameters, arguments-before-name, multiple calls, incomplete payloads, inter-tool whitespace, Anthropic streaming, and token metadata.
- Update the parser benchmark to generate protocol-correct fixtures, respect tokenizer-valid marker boundaries, and validate streaming/complete results before recording timings.

## BC-breaking (Optional)

There are no request-schema or CLI flag changes. However, this PR intentionally changes the parser extension API and several edge-case output semantics:

- Custom `ToolParser` implementations must migrate from `start_tool_call()`, `finish_tool_call()`, `decode_tool_incremental()`, `parse_tool_call_complete()`, `validate_complete()`, and `get_tool_payload_format()` to the consumed-prefix interface based on `begin_tool_block()`, `feed_tool_block()`, and `_consume_stream_payload()`.
- `ProtocolProfile`, `ResponseParser.profile`, and `ResponseParser.validate_complete()` are removed. The server no longer rewrites `stop`/`length` to `parse_error` based on terminal parser validation. Consumers requiring strict argument validation should validate returned tool calls themselves.
- `lmdeploy.serve.parsers.tool_parser.qwen2d5_tool_parser.Qwen2d5ToolParser` is removed. The `qwen2d5` registry name remains supported and resolves to `Qwen3ToolParser`; downstream Python imports should migrate to `Qwen3ToolParser`.
- Streaming consumers now always receive the function identity before argument fragments.
- Empty SSE deltas and newlines between adjacent tool calls may no longer be emitted. When one engine chunk produces multiple parser deltas, its token IDs and logprobs are emitted only once.
- Tool names absent from the request's tool list are now filtered consistently across built-in tool parsers.

title: fix(serve): wait for XML tool name before streaming arguments
body:
## Motivation

For the XML tool protocol (`qwen3coder` and friends), the streaming parser can emit
argument deltas before the function name has been parsed out of the incoming text.

This is harmless for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but it breaks the Anthropic
adapter: a `tool_use` content block must be opened with a non-empty `id` and `name`.
When an argument-only delta arrives first, the adapter opens a `content_block_start`
whose identity fields are empty, which Anthropic-compatible clients reject.

The failure is easy to hit with malformed or truncated XML, e.g. a `<tool_call>`
that carries `<parameter=...>` but never produces a well-formed function header:

```text
</think><tool_call><parameter=query>nvd zabbix</parameter>
```

## Modification

- `XmlToolParser.decode_tool_incremental`: keep parsed arguments in the incremental state
  until the function name has been emitted. Argument deltas are still emitted normally
  once the name delta has gone out, so well-formed streams are unaffected.
- Add regression tests:
  - `test_qwen3_5_parser.py`: incomplete XML function headers must not produce
    argument deltas ahead of the name.
  - `test_endpoints.py`: a malformed XML tool call must not open a `tool_use` block
    with empty identity, and the response is reported as `parse_error`.

## BC-breaking (Optional)

No. Well-formed tool calls produce the same delta sequence as before; only the
ordering of the first argument delta relative to the name delta changes, and only
for streams that previously produced an invalid Anthropic block.

title: fix(serve): emit signatures for Anthropic thinking blocks
body:
## Motivation

Anthropic-compatible responses currently omit the `signature` field from thinking blocks.

Clients may replay assistant thinking blocks in subsequent requests and expect each block to contain a signature. For streaming responses, the Anthropic protocol delivers the signature through a `signature_delta` event immediately before `content_block_stop`.

This PR adds a local opaque signature marker so that LMDeploy-generated thinking blocks can be replayed by Anthropic-compatible clients.

## Modification

- Add `signature` to non-streaming thinking blocks.
- Emit one `signature_delta` before closing each streaming thinking block.
- Keep `content_block_start` unchanged and only emit signatures for thinking blocks.

## Summary

title: feat(pytorch): add piecewise CUDA graph prefill
body:
## Motivation

LMDeploy currently captures decode with a full CUDA graph, but prefill often cannot be captured as one graph because attention metadata, recurrent-state updates, sparse attention, and DeepEP collectives depend on live request or distributed state.

Running the entire prefill eagerly leaves graph-safe projections, normalization, tensor transformations, and local MoE work paying Python and kernel-launch overhead.

This PR adds an opt-in piecewise CUDA graph (PCG) path that captures graph-safe regions while executing graph-hostile operators eagerly in their original order:

```text
GraphPiece -> EagerCall -> GraphPiece -> ...
```

The implementation uses direct CUDA capture. It does not depend on `torch.compile`, Dynamo graph breaks, or FX partitioning.

## Modification

### Graph-runner architecture

- Refactor the CUDA graph runner into:
  - `runner.py`: eager/full-graph/piecewise dispatch;
  - `full_graph.py`: existing full decode CUDA graph behavior;
  - `piecewise.py`: generic tracing, stable bridges, ordered replay, streams, and plan ownership;
  - `standard.py`: standard-decoder token buckets, input padding, output slicing, and request selection.
- Keep the existing full CUDA graph decode path unchanged.
- Add a graph-runner README describing ownership, lifecycle, extension points, and unsupported cases.

### Piecewise capture and replay

- Capture contiguous graph-safe CUDA work around explicitly registered eager boundaries.
- Preserve eager calls and graph pieces in their original execution order.
- Bind request-local eager arguments by exact execution-frame identity.
- Use stable, runner-owned bridge storage for eager outputs consumed by later graph pieces.
- Share one ordered CUDA stream across mutually exclusive PCG plans while retaining independent CUDA graph-private pools.
- Add profiler ranges for complete PCG replay and individual graph/eager steps.

### Startup and configuration

- Capture every supported token bucket during startup warmup.
- Never capture or evict plans during serving.
- Add `PytorchEngineConfig.piecewise_cudagraph_max_tokens`.
  - `None` keeps PCG disabled.
  - A positive value enables PCG and sets its maximum prefill-token cutoff.
  - Requests above the cutoff remain eager.
- Expose the setting through `lmdeploy serve api_server` and `benchmark/profile_throughput.py`.
- Keep PCG policy independent of scheduler and paging capacity.

### Operator and model integration

CUDA implementations own their eager boundaries and output adapters; the generic graph runner contains no model- or operator-specific dispatch.

Initial integration covers:

- default and FA3 attention;
- MLA and NSA/DSA paths;
- causal convolution and gated-delta-rule state updates;
- local and DeepEP MoE implementations;
- Qwen3, Qwen3.5, and GLM MoE DSA model families;
- TP and supported DP/EP execution;
- Qwen3.5 MTP under TP2 and DP2/EP4.

Unsupported operator or topology combinations fail closed and use eager execution. `DP_TP` layer execution remains explicitly unsupported.

### Distributed failure handling

If Ray executor initialization fails while constructing distributed graph state, all worker actors are terminated and the original initialization exception is preserved.

## Usage

```bash
lmdeploy serve api_server Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
    --backend pytorch \
    --piecewise-cudagraph-max-tokens 512
```

The cutoff should be selected using measurements for the target model, backend, and hardware. Larger buckets can lose performance because of padded computation and eager-to-graph bridge copies.

## Validation

### Real-model validation

- Qwen3-8B showed about 27% lower p50 end-to-end latency for the tested 512-token H200 workload.
- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 with MTP completed:
  - TP2 serving;
  - DP2/EP4 serving with DeepEP;
  - a 2,000-request mixed-prefill soak at concurrency 32;
  - 1,037,626 prompt tokens and 128,000 completion tokens without HTTP, CUDA, NCCL, DeepEP, or bridge-shape failures.
- Full `GPQA_diamond_repeat_4` completed all 792 generations under both TP2 and DP2/EP4 without serving or judge failures.

## Known limitations

- Token-bucket padding can change floating-point reduction shapes, so padded PCG output is not necessarily bitwise identical to raw-shape eager output. Mechanism comparisons use an equivalent bucket-shaped eager baseline.
- Captured plans remain resident for the runner lifetime and increase startup time and CUDA graph memory usage.
- Runtime capture, plan eviction, concurrent replay on one runner, `DP_TP`, and PCG on PyTorch 2.0 are not supported.

title: fix(deps): pin xgrammar below 0.2.5.post1 to unbreak unit-test CI
body:
## Motivation

Since 2026-09-03 ~07:02 UTC, every PR's `unit-test` workflow fails with:

```
ImportError: please install latest transformers by pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git
```

- 8 errors in `tests/test_lmdeploy/test_mtp_guided_decoding.py`: building `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` calls `check_transformers()` in `lmdeploy/vl/model/qwen3_5.py`, which requires `transformers.models.qwen3_5.*` (transformers >= 5.16).
- 1 failure in `tests/pytorch/config/test_hf_overrides.py:26`: `hf_config.text_config.rope_parameters` was renamed from `rope_scaling` in transformers 5.x.

Root cause: xgrammar **0.2.5.post1** was published at 2026-09-03 07:02 UTC and introduced `transformers<5` as a hard dependency ([PyPI metadata](https://pypi.org/project/xgrammar/0.2.5.post1/)):

| | xgrammar <= 0.2.5 | xgrammar 0.2.5.post1 | xgrammar 0.2.6rc* |
|---|---|---|---|
| transformers dep | `>=4.38.0` | `<5,>=4.38.0` | `>=4.38.0` (reverted) |

Because `requirements/common.txt` pins `xgrammar >= 0.1.33` with no constraint on the upper side, pip always picks the newest xgrammar and is then forced to downgrade transformers to **4.57.6** (the newest <5 release), which lacks the `qwen3_5` module and breaks `test_hf_overrides`.

Verified against two unit-test runs from the same day: the run at 06:49 UTC resolved `xgrammar-0.2.3 + transformers-5.16.1` (2066 passed); runs after 07:02 UTC resolved `xgrammar-0.2.5.post1 + transformers-4.57.6` (8 errors, 1 failure).

## Modification

Exclude only the broken release instead of adding an upper bound, so future releases resolve automatically once they fix the dependency (0.2.6rc already reverts to `transformers>=4.38.0`); no follow-up PR needed. Style follows the `transformers` line in the same file.

```diff
--- requirements/common.txt
-xgrammar >= 0.1.33
+xgrammar >= 0.1.33, != 0.2.5.post1
```

## Checklist

1. ✅ No lint issues introduced (one-line dependency pin change).
2. ✅ Covered by existing unit tests — this fix restores the environment the existing suite already expects (transformers 5.16.1, as in the 06:49 UTC run).
3. ✅ Verified via `packaging` specifier check: `0.1.33`–`0.2.5` and hypothetical `0.2.6` are allowed, only `0.2.5.post1` is excluded.
4. ✅ No documentation changes needed (no user-facing API change).

title: fix: initialize MLA KV-B after online FP8 quantization
body:
## Summary

- load MLA `kv_b_proj` through the standard quant-aware linear path
- materialize the absorbed `kc`/`vc` BMM weights after linear weight processing completes
- reuse the two-phase post-load lifecycle for initial loading and online weight updates

## Motivation

When online FP8 is applied to a BF16 checkpoint, the previous special KV-B loader treated `kv_b_proj.weight` as serialized FP8 and waited for a checkpoint `weight_scale_inv`. Online quantization generates that scale instead, so the expected checkpoint scale never arrived and the derived `kc`/`vc` weights could remain uninitialized.

Routing KV-B through the standard linear loader lets it create the effective FP8 weight and scales. A second post-load pass then materializes the BF16 MLA BMM weights from that effective representation, matching the lifecycle used by vLLM.

## Validation

- existing focused PyTorch tests: 15 passed
- pre-commit hooks on all changed files: passed
